title: Does Islam allow people to do whatever they want?
headline: Quran and hadith place human freedom inside obedience to God's commands

summary.text: The Quran asks whether man will be left neglected, and its tafsir explains this as being left with no command, prohibition or reckoning. The Prophet ﷺ said everyone of his Ummah will enter Paradise except those who refuse, and he explained that refusing means disobeying him. The answer concludes that the permissible is wide but no one may declare the unlawful lawful or the lawful forbidden.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 7280: Holding Fast to the Qur'an and Sunnah

paragraphs.text: The Quran poses the question directly: "Does man think that he will be left neglected?" (Quran 75:36). Its tafsir spells out the sense as being left with no command, no prohibition and no reckoning.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Everyone of my Ummah will enter Paradise except those who refuse." When asked who would refuse, he said: "He who obeys me will enter Paradise, and who disobeys me has refused." The scholars graded this report authentic (Sahih al-Bukhari 7280).
The freedom to choose among what is lawful is real, but it sits inside obedience. There is wide room to choose among the lawful, and no room to declare the unlawful lawful or the lawful forbidden.
